statements.action_statement: What: Accepts CVE-2026-14456 (OpenSSL QUIC-server unbounded-memory- growth DoS) as tracked risk for `libssl3`/`libcrypto3` across every Alpine-based first-party image (transitive dependency of `apk-tools` itself, present regardless of any image's own TLS/QUIC usage). Why: Time-boxed maintainer-authorized exception while the apk-upgrade cache-bust fix (PR #1680, merged 2026-08-26T12:01:29Z) propagates through every affected image's next rebuild; no `paths:` scoping applies since Trivy's Alpine os-pkgs finding class carries no PkgPath. None of this project's services run a QUIC server. Re-verified 2026-08-27 (not yet removable): every first-party GHCR `:nightly` tag checked (`proxy`/`dhcp`/`ntp`/`dhcp-proxy`/ `dns`/`syslog`/`watchdog`/`utilities`/`ui`/`build-tools`; `netdata` excluded -- `gh api users/wiki-mod/packages?package_type=container` confirms `lancache-ng/netdata` is not among this org's published GHCR packages, so it isn't a first-party image to check here) has a `docker inspect` `.Created` timestamp between 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-16, all before the PR Trivy scan of `ui:nightly` (Alpine 3.24.1) without `--ignore- unfixed`/`--trivyignores` confirms the finding is real and fixed upstream but not yet in the built image: `CVE-2026-14456` `libssl3`/`libcrypto3`, `FixedVersion: 3.5.8-r0`. Re-check after the next rebuild of all listed images. Scope correction (found 2026-08-27, not previously documented): since this entry has no `paths:` key, it is not actually Alpine-only in effect -- a same-CVE-ID live finding also exists on `tools/build-tools`'s Debian `openssl`/`libssl3t64`/ `openssl-provider-legacy`/`libssl-dev` packages (`FixedVersion: 3.5.7-1~deb13u2`, confirmed via a live Trivy scan of `build-tools:nightly` without `--ignore-unfixed`/`--trivyignores`) and is being suppressed by this same entry as a side effect. PR `tools/build-tools`'s Debian `apt`-upgrade path has an equivalent staleness problem remains unverified and needs its own check. From: Issue #1095, PR #1685

statements.impact_statement: What: Suppresses CVE-2026-34040 (a Docker daemon authorization-plugin bypass) for docker-compose/docker-buildx; anchor entry for the docker/docker client-library-only group (CVE-2026-41567/42306 below share this background). Why: Vulnerable code not present -- the fix is daemon-side pkg/authorization middleware; docker-buildx embeds github.com/docker/docker only as an API client library and never compiles it. Re-verified 2026-09-05 for the prebuilt binaries: docker/buildx v0.37.0's vendor/modules.txt lists only github.com/docker/docker/pkg/namesgenerator, so the middleware is absent, while docker/compose v5.5.1 no longer vendors github.com/docker/docker at all (migrated to github.com/moby/moby/api), so the docker-compose path is retained only as a harmless obsolete anchor. This advisory affects moby/moby < 29.3.1 rather than docker/docker; whether Trivy still reports it against docker-buildx MUST be re-checked on the post-switch image's live scan. From: Issue #1304, PR #1548

What: Suppresses CVE-2026-41567 (a Docker daemon `docker cp`/archive- upload host code execution finding) for docker-compose/docker-buildx. Why: Same docker/docker client-library-only disposition as CVE-2026-34040 above. This is server-side request-handling code in the daemon's archive handler; docker/buildx v0.37.0's vendor/modules.txt vendors only pkg/namesgenerator, confirming the handler is absent (re-verified 2026-09-05 for the prebuilt v0.37.0 binary, which still vendors docker/docker v28.5.2 with no fixed release; docker/compose v5.5.1 no longer vendors docker/docker). From: Issue #1304, PR #1548

What: Suppresses CVE-2026-42306 (GHSA-rg2x-37c3-w2rh, a Docker daemon `docker cp` bind-mount race condition) for docker-compose/docker-buildx. Why: Same docker/docker client-library-only disposition as CVE-2026-34040 above. This is a race condition in the daemon's own `docker cp` implementation; confirmed absent by the same vendor/modules.txt check (re-verified 2026-09-05 for the prebuilt docker/buildx v0.37.0 binary; docker/compose v5.5.1 no longer vendors docker/docker). From: Issue #1304, PR #1548

What: Suppresses CVE-2026-17106 (GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h, a github.com/moby/go-archive path-traversal/link-following flaw in the Untar/Unpack/ApplyLayer archive-extraction functions) for the prebuilt docker-buildx plugin. Why: Vulnerable code not present -- docker/buildx v0.37.0's vendor/modules.txt vendors only the go-archive/compression subpackage, not the root `archive` package that defines the affected Untar/Unpack/ApplyLayer functions, so the flawed code is never compiled into the binary. The module floors at v0.2.0 (transitively via moby/buildkit) below the v0.3.0 fix, but a scanner keys on that module version, not on reachable code. It is a build-time-only CI tool over trusted input regardless (AV:L/UI:R). From: Issue #1671

statements.action_statement: What: Accepts CVE-2026-12064 (an SSH host-verification bypass via schemeless SFTP/SCP URLs) as tracked risk for `libcurl4t64` in `tools/build-tools`. Anchor entry for this file's curl group (CVE-2026-8286/8458/8927/8932/9079/9080/9545/10536 below). Why: Trivy reports `Status: affected`, `FixedVersion: None`; no `paths:` scoping applies since Trivy's Debian os-pkgs finding class carries no `PkgPath`. This file's from-source curl/git build purges Debian's `curl`/`libcurl3t64-gnutls` entirely; `libcurl4t64` remains solely as `cmake`'s package dependency (`apt-get autoremove` strips cmake once it's purged) and drives only already-vendored C/C++ builds (e.g. aws-lc-sys/BoringSSL for services/ui), never a network fetch. Verified via a real Trivy scan of the current image (2026-08-24, lancache-229): every finding in this group attributes solely to `libcurl4t64`; `curl`/ `libcurl3t64-gnutls` no longer appear at all. Debian trixie fix status individually re-checked against security-tracker.debian.org on 2026-08-27 for all 9 IDs in this group, including CVE-2026-8458/10536: all still `vulnerable`/`no-dsa` at curl 8.14.1-2+deb13u4 -- a same-day batch source-package-tracker query misreported CVE-2026-9079/9080 as "fixed"; each CVE's own tracker page was re-fetched individually and both confirm `vulnerable`. Caveat: this session's own live Trivy scans (elsewhere in this audit) predate the libcurl4t64-only purge above (2026-08-24 per that note, checked 2026-08-27) -- not re-run against the post-purge image; the Debian trixie fix status itself is unaffected by which package Trivy currently attributes the finding to. From: Issue #1304, PR #1661

What: Accepts CVE-2026-8286 (an insecure TLS-configuration-mismatch connection issue) as tracked risk for `libcurl4t64` in `tools/build-tools`. Why: Same curl finding group as CVE-2026-12064 above; `Status: affected`, severity HIGH, cmake's unexercised transitive dependency only (verified 2026-08-24, lancache-229). From: Issue #1304, PR #1661

What: Accepts CVE-2026-8458 (a Negotiate-authentication connection- reuse logical error letting a request reuse the wrong connection) as tracked risk for `libcurl4t64` in `tools/build-tools`. Why: Same curl finding group as CVE-2026-12064 above; requires an application to actually make Negotiate-authenticated requests through libcurl's connection pool, which cmake's unexercised transitive dependency never does (verified 2026-08-24, lancache-229). From: Issue #1304, PR #1661

What: Accepts CVE-2026-8927 (a proxy-authentication-state information-disclosure issue) as tracked risk for `libcurl4t64` in `tools/build-tools`. Why: Same curl finding group as CVE-2026-12064 above; `Status: affected`, severity HIGH, cmake's unexercised transitive dependency only (verified 2026-08-24, lancache-229). From: Issue #1304, PR #1661

What: Accepts CVE-2026-8932 (an mTLS-connection-reuse security-feature-bypass issue) as tracked risk for `libcurl4t64` in `tools/build-tools`. Why: Same curl finding group as CVE-2026-12064 above; reclassified to `Severity: MEDIUM`, cmake's unexercised transitive dependency only (verified 2026-08-24, lancache-229). From: Issue #1304, PR #1661

From: Issue #1304, PR #1661

What: Accepts CVE-2026-9080 (a `curl_easy_pause()` use-after-free reachable via a libcurl multi-interface callback) as tracked risk for `libcurl4t64` in `tools/build-tools`. Why: Same curl finding group as CVE-2026-12064 above; the vulnerable `CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION` callback API is never used -- cmake's unexercised transitive dependency only (verified 2026-08-24, lancache-229). From: Issue #1304, PR #1661

What: Accepts CVE-2026-9545 (a cached-SSL-session-and-early-data information-disclosure issue) as tracked risk for `libcurl4t64` in `tools/build-tools`. Why: Same curl finding group as CVE-2026-12064 above; reachable only across a long-lived process reusing a cached session, which does not describe cmake's unexercised transitive dependency (verified 2026-08-24, lancache-229). From: Issue #1304, PR #1661

What: Accepts CVE-2026-10536 (a use-after-free in libcurl's HTTP/2 stream-dependency handling, reachable via `CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS`/ `CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E` followed by `curl_easy_reset()` and `curl_easy_cleanup()`) as tracked risk for `libcurl4t64` in `tools/build-tools`. Why: Same curl finding group as CVE-2026-12064 above; requires an application to actually set HTTP/2 stream-dependency options via libcurl's easy-handle API, which cmake's unexercised transitive dependency never does (verified 2026-08-24, lancache-229). Newly surfaced by this scan; not present in the prior curl-group review. From: Issue #1304, PR #1661

statements.impact_statement: What: Marks CVE-2011-4116 (`perl-base`'s `File::Temp` module creating temporary files insecurely) as not exploitable in `services/ui` and `tools/build-tools`. Anchor entry for a 30-ID group spanning the Debian `perl-base`, util-linux, ncurses, `gzip`, and `libacl1` package groups. Why: All 30 are `Priority: required`/`Essential: yes` Debian packages or their hard link-time dependents, so none can be purged; "not exploitable" is the only available disposition short of migrating the image off Debian. Neither image invokes Perl at all (grep-confirmed; re-verified 2026-08-19 against the current tree; re-confirmed 2026-08-27 via a fresh grep against origin/current_dev: zero `perl`/`setfacl`/`getfacl`/`chfn`/`chsh`/`gzexe`/`mount` invocations in `services/ui`/`tools/build-tools`; no ncurses-linked crate in `services/ui/Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`; `services/ui`'s privilege drop uses `setpriv`, confirmed live in `services/ui/docker-entrypoint.sh`). Applicability flag (found 2026-08-27, not resolved here): `services/ui/Dockerfile`'s final stage is `FROM mirror.gcr.io/library/alpine:3.24`, and every Trivy scan of a first-party service in this repo's CI (`trivy-scan-exact-digest` in build-push.yml/build-push-hosted-fallback.yml) targets the exact pushed final-stage digest, never an intermediate build stage. A live scan of `ui:nightly` confirms Trivy detects it as `alpine 3.24.1`, not Debian -- none of this 30-ID group's Debian package names can appear in that scan's `os-pkgs` findings at all. This group may therefore no longer need `services/ui` in its applicability claim (only `tools/build-tools`, confirmed Debian and confirmed still matching several of these IDs live, e.g. CVE-2026-13221/CVE-2026-8376/CVE-2026-42496/CVE-2026-42497/ CVE-2026-9538/CVE-2026-54369/CVE-2025-69720/CVE-2026-41992 in a 2026-08-27 full-severity, no-ignorefile scan of `build-tools: nightly`) -- not changed in this pass since it doesn't affect whether these 30 entries stay or go, flagged for the maintainer to confirm/correct the wording. From: Issue #815, PR #1454, Issue #1598

statements.action_statement: What: Accepts CVE-2026-41991 (an arbitrary-file-overwrite via insecure temporary-file handling in the `gzexe` utility) as tracked risk for `tools/build-tools` only; `services/ui` is unaffected. Anchor entry for the 2-ID gzip group (this and CVE-2026-41992 below) -- the only ID in this file's 30-ID batch where the two images' exploitability genuinely differs. Why: `services/ui` never invokes `gzip`/`gzexe` (grep-confirmed). Trivy's finding applies per-CVE-ID repo-wide with no per-image `paths:` scoping for Debian os-pkgs, so the disposition reflects the more exploitable image: `tools/build-tools` unpacks pinned, checksum-verified release tarballs via `gzip`, never invoking `gzexe` itself or on attacker-supplied input. No `trixie`/ `trixie-backports` fix exists yet (Debian security-tracker: only `sid` has 1.14-1; re-verified 2026-08-19; re-confirmed 2026-08-27 against security-tracker.debian.org: trixie gzip 1.13-1 remains `vulnerable` for both CVE-2026-41991 and CVE-2026-41992, fix only in sid 1.14-1). From: Issue #815, PR #1454, Issue #1598

What: Accepts CVE-2026-41992 (a global buffer overflow in gzip's own LZH decompression path -- legacy `.lzh`/SCO-compress-format support) as tracked risk for `tools/build-tools` only; the HIGH-severity ID in this group. Why: Same gzip finding group as CVE-2026-41991 above. `tools/build-tools`'s `gzip` usage (unpacking plain `.tar.gz` tarballs) never exercises the LZH code path, which only triggers on input explicitly identified as LZH-formatted. From: Issue #815, PR #1454, Issue #1598

statements.impact_statement: What: Suppresses CVE-2026-27145 (Go stdlib crypto/x509 DoS via excessive DNS SAN processing) for actionlint's release binary. Anchor entry for a 20-ID embedded-Go-stdlib group (the 19 sibling entries below share this background) -- actionlint v1.7.12's official release binary statically embeds a Go stdlib older than the fixes for all 20 IDs, confirmed by a real Trivy scan (aquasec/trivy v0.74.0, vulnerability DB updated 2026-08-28T17:56Z) of tools/build-tools's built image on 2026-08-28. Why: All 20 IDs in this group are DoS/parsing findings in networking-adjacent stdlib packages (crypto/tls, crypto/x509, net, net/http, net/mail, net/url, mime, encoding/xml, encoding/asn1, html/template, golang.org/x/net). tools/build-tools invokes actionlint only for a fully offline static lint of local workflow YAML files (actionlint <file>..., per AG-VAL-017/AG-CI-001) -- that invocation never opens a TLS/HTTP connection, resolves DNS, or parses an attacker-supplied email/MIME/XML/HTML document, so none of this group's vulnerable code paths is reachable from how this project actually runs the tool. Per the rewritten AG-KD-003 (PR exemption precisely because its vulnerable code is unreachable in this invocation -- this is a reachability finding, not a general accepted-risk waiver. From: Issue #1095, PR #1743

What: Suppresses CVE-2026-32280 (crypto/tls DoS via certificate chain building) for actionlint's release binary. Why: Same embedded-Go-stdlib disposition as CVE-2026-27145 above. TLS certificate-chain building is never exercised by this project's offline lint invocation. From: Issue #1095, PR #1743

What: Suppresses CVE-2026-32281 (crypto/x509 DoS via inefficient certificate chain validation) for actionlint's release binary. Why: Same embedded-Go-stdlib disposition as CVE-2026-27145 above.
